scope: Regular room-enemy lifecycle: player pursuit target acquisition, actor AI callback self-modification, actor-data spawn staging, and the ordinary health-zero entry. Established while building room-scoped enemy state/health/AI synchronization against a live two-client build.
game: Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon (US rev1) recompilation

nativeEvidence.finding: Room enemies acquire "the player" through the current player display object at 0x801FC60C. The position is read either directly, through the player task 0x801FC604 at +0x18 (same object), or through the actor target-object field at +0x84 consumed by func_802197D8. Writing the object's +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 during a single actor's AI callback redirects that actor's pursuit; restoring immediately afterwards leaves the local player's own update, collision, rendering and camera unaffected.
nativeEvidence.method: Ghidra decompilation of the target helper plus live two-client behavior: moving the object for one actor's callback caused that actor to pursue the redirected position while the local player never observed the temporary transform.

nativeEvidence.finding: The scheduler invokes callbacks at task +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 and inhibits a callback address carrying bit 0x00800000. Ordinary actors use +0x0C as a self-modifying AI state callback: a state transition rewrites +0x0C to the next callback. Temporarily replacing an actor's +0x0C to scope work (hold or wrap) therefore requires saving the replaced callback, invoking it, and restoring only while +0x0C still equals the replacement, while preserving the inhibit tag so paused/cutscene actors stay paused.
nativeEvidence.method: Ghidra decompilation and live behavior across two-client sessions; a trampoline that preserved the tag and restored conditionally did not break enemy state transitions.

nativeEvidence.finding: Static room actors are staged by func_8020D848_5C8D18, which selects the per-room metadata record at D_80231300_5EC7D0[room]. A record exposes the normal actor-instance array, partitioned/proximity lists, and the actor-data file id; a zero instance definition terminates each list. func_80218A54 initializes each instance and updates the transient scratch pointers D_8015CDDC (current instance) and D_8015CDE0 (resolved definition).
nativeEvidence.method: Ghidra decompilation of the spawn stage/initializer plus a room roster enumeration that reproduced the actor counts and signed signature across two clients.

nativeEvidence.finding: func_80218548_5D3A18 is entered only from the common zero-health path, not by scene unloads or distance culls, making it the authoritative local death edge for an ordinary actor. Setting health (task +0x8D) to one and status bit 0x00040000 reproduces the real zero-health reaction, counters, effects and cleanup through the normal damage pipeline.
nativeEvidence.method: Ghidra decompilation and live single/two-client tests where a synthetic fast-hit produced the native death animation, drop and removal.

limitations: Player-object relocation was confirmed for the inspected room actors; not every actor was enumerated. An actor that caches the player task pointer and reads task-only fields, or uses a separate hard-coded player structure, may not follow the redirected position.
Target selection in the mod chooses the nearest candidate per actor with no hysteresis; this is a mod policy, not native behavior.
Enemy-owned attack tasks/projectiles were not part of these findings and are not documented here.
The health/transform/target behavior is scoped to US rev1 and the inspected overlay/actor set.
supportingSource: mnsg-recomp-example native room-enemy synchronization module and its documentation; findings cross-checked against current Ghidra decompilation of the resident helpers and live two-client sessions.
